Stack Map and Labs

Each box is a component you are likely to draw in a system design interview, placed where it sits on the path of a request. Tap a box to see what it does, what it connects to, and where to read more. Boxes with a ring on the corner open a deeper interactive view. The hands-on labs below the map show how to run the main components on a Windows machine with WSL 2 and how to operate them.

Highlight a route
request path lookup or side call opens a deeper view

Hands-on labs

Each lab runs part of the stack on a Windows machine with WSL 2. A lab lists its files, how to start it, how to operate it, exercises, and fixes for common errors. Do them in order. The Learning Path page gives the order to follow, unit by unit.

Updated October 13, 2026: Labs 6 to 8, reliability between systems: the outbox, a job status with a heartbeat and a sweeper, and a payment with an outside processor and an idempotency key. They extend the stack-lab project of Labs 1 and 2 with a scheduler and a processor stand-in. Earlier the same day: Lab 5, Receiving events, with webhooks; Lab 4, Data for integrations; and Lab 3, Outside APIs, with a stand-in for the GitHub REST API. October 12, 2026: an Explain button on every command block, with a map of the parts the command reaches; a Commands tab in each lab; and additions to Lab 0 for machines that already have Docker Desktop.
